questions.q: What is the key difference between how a Power Automate flow and a Copilot Studio agent handle a task?
options: A flow is deterministic and always follows the exact path you designed; an agent reasons about the request and decides its own path
A flow can only run on a schedule, while an agent can only run from a chat message
There is no real difference — they are the same engine with a different name
An agent can never call a connector, while a flow can only call connectors
questions.explain: A flow always takes the exact path you designed. An agent is reasoning-driven: given instructions, knowledge, and tools, it decides at runtime what to do based on the actual request.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three things you can build in Copilot Studio?
options: Agents
Workflows
Agent flows
Power BI dashboards
questions.explain: Copilot Studio's three building blocks are agents, workflows, and agent flows. Power BI dashboards are a separate Microsoft product, not something Copilot Studio builds.

questions.q: How can an agent flow be used, according to this lesson?
options: Only as a standalone automation that can never connect to an agent
Only as a replacement for Power Automate itself
It can run standalone, or be attached to an agent as a tool the agent calls when it needs to
It can only be triggered manually by an administrator
questions.explain: An agent flow can run on its own, or it can be attached to an agent as a tool — this is the bridge between Copilot Studio agents and flow-style automation.

questions.q: What is a "harness" in Copilot Studio?
options: A physical device used to connect Power Automate to Azure
The underlying engine that governs how an agent or workflow reasons, how complex a task it can take on, and how it's billed
A type of knowledge source an agent can connect to
The name for a published agent's public URL
questions.explain: A harness is the engine behind whatever you build in Copilot Studio — it shapes reasoning ability, complexity, and billing. The standard harness is the one this chapter focuses on.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say your Power Automate skills from Chapters 1 and 2 "don't go to waste" in Copilot Studio?
options: Because Copilot Studio is actually just a rebranded version of Power Automate with no differences
Because agent flows use the same trigger-and-action mental model you already learned, and later lessons connect an agent directly to flow-style automation
Because you must rebuild every flow from Chapters 1 and 2 before Copilot Studio will work
Because knowledge of JSON is required to sign in to Copilot Studio
questions.explain: Agent flows use the same trigger-and-action structure as Power Automate cloud flows, and this chapter builds toward connecting an agent directly to that kind of automation.
